security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily Markdown guidance for running Google Nano Banana 2 through the RunComfy CLI. Confirmed risks are limited to disclosed external CLI execution and outbound RunComfy API access; most static hits are false positives from code fences, tables, links, or security documentation.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution is central to the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the command arguments structured as JSON, require user confirmation before running generation jobs, and avoid interpolating untrusted text into shell syntax.

remediation.issue: RunComfy credentials are required for authenticated use.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI and remind users not to paste tokens into prompts, logs, or generated examples.

remediation.issue: Generated outputs are downloaded from remote RunComfy domains.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the documented output-domain whitelist and file-size cap, and store generated files only in user-selected output directories.

content.user_title: Generate Nano Banana 2 Images on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Image teams need quick drafts without rewriting model-specific prompts each time. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to run Nano Banana 2 through RunComfy with practical image settings.
actual_capabilities: Runs the RunComfy Nano Banana 2 text-to-image endpoint through the local CLI.
Shows request options for prompt, image count, seed, aspect ratio, resolution, output format, and safety tolerance.
Provides command patterns for drafts, batch ideation, seed-locked finals, and web-grounded prompts.
Explains when to choose Nano Banana 2 instead of related image models or edit endpoints.
Documents CLI exit codes, authentication options, outbound endpoints, and output download behavior.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and an authenticated RunComfy account or token.
Only supports still image generation through this endpoint, not video or image editing.
Each request supports at most four generated images.
Higher resolutions and web search can increase cost and latency.

use_cases.title: Create social campaign drafts
use_cases.description: Generate multiple vertical or square image options for rapid social media review.

use_cases.title: Prototype product cards
use_cases.description: Use quoted in-image text and consistent framing to draft e-commerce cards or promotional assets.

use_cases.title: Prepare web-grounded visuals
use_cases.description: Enable web search when prompts reference current events, public entities, or recent context.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner square draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple one-image draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 1K square PNG with Nano Banana 2: a clean studio image of [subject], [style], [lighting], [background]. Save it to my chosen output folder.

prompt_templates.title: Batch ideation set
prompt_templates.scenario: Explore four fast variants before selecting a final direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana 2 to create four 0.5K images in 9:16 format for [campaign]. Keep the subject first, use [visual style], and make each option suitable for mobile review.

prompt_templates.title: Seed-locked refinement
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine one composition while keeping framing stable.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 2K 16:9 final with Nano Banana 2 using seed [number]. Keep the same composition, improve [detail], and include the exact text "[text]" in [placement].

prompt_templates.title: Web-grounded current visual
prompt_templates.scenario: Use fresh public context for a time-sensitive image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana 2 with web search enabled for a prompt about [current event or real entity]. Create one 1K image that is accurate, neutral, and suitable for editorial planning.

output_examples.input: Create four mobile thumbnails for a wellness tea launch.
output: Four 9:16 draft images are generated at 0.5K resolution.
The prompts emphasize the product, lighting, calm styling, and mobile-safe framing.
The files are saved in the requested output directory.

output_examples.input: Make a product card that says "Brewed Quietly".
output: A 16:9 image is generated with the quoted text placed clearly in the composition.
The result uses clean studio lighting and negative space for e-commerce review.

output_examples.input: Generate a current-event concept image with web grounding.
output: The request enables web search for fresh context.
The result is downloaded from the RunComfy output domain into the selected folder.

best_practices: Put the main subject first, then describe action, environment, style, and camera details.
Quote exact in-image text and specify its placement, size, and visual style.
Use 0.5K for exploration, 1K for normal drafts, and higher resolutions only for final assets.
anti_patterns: Do not use this text-to-image endpoint for image edits that need preserved subject identity.
Do not combine many conflicting styles in one prompt.
Do not enable web search unless the prompt needs current public context.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates still images with the RunComfy Nano Banana 2 text-to-image endpoint.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the RunComfy CLI and either an interactive login or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: No. This skill targets text-to-image generation. Use a separate edit endpoint for image edits.

faq.question: How many images can it create per request?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint supports one to four images per request.

faq.question: When should I enable web search?
faq.answer: Enable it only when the prompt refers to current events, real entities, or recent public context.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
